foam-verify 0.0.1, from `study.toml`: 4 levels, finest first; refined = mesh; grid sequence structured; refined directions d = 2; formal order 2.

## Verdict

**Not a clean pass.** 0 of 1 quantity of interest are clean passes.

| QoI | Finest grid | Relative U | Grid convergence | Clean pass |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `u(y=0.8516)` | 0.235341 +/- 0.000127 | 0.054% | monotonic, p = 2.279 | no |

What stops a clean pass:

- `u(y=0.8516)`: level 160x160: drifting: over the last 20 samples (x = 0.05 to 1): relative range 1.36, relative drift 0.901; the drift exceeds tol = 0.001, so the QoI is still changing
- `u(y=0.8516)`: level 80x80: drifting: over the last 20 samples (x = 0.05 to 1): relative range 1.35, relative drift 0.898; the drift exceeds tol = 0.001, so the QoI is still changing
- `u(y=0.8516)`: level 40x40: drifting: over the last 20 samples (x = 0.05 to 1): relative range 1.34, relative drift 0.888; the drift exceeds tol = 0.001, so the QoI is still changing

## Levels

| Level | Folder | Cells | r to the next coarser |
|---|---|---|---|
| 160x160 | `n160` | 25,600 | 2.000 |
| 80x80 | `n80` | 6,400 | 2.000 |
| 40x40 | `n40` | 1,600 | 2.000 |
| 20x20 | `n20` | 400 |  |

## Settings consistency

**Pass.** No difference blocks a clean pass; the differences below are noted.

Compared on every level: `system/fvSchemes`, `system/fvSolution`, `constant/transportProperties`, `0/U`, `0/p`, `system/controlDict`.

| File | Entry | 160x160 | 80x80 | 40x40 | 20x20 | Blocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `system/controlDict` | `deltaT` | 0.0003125 | 0.000625 | 0.00125 | 0.0025 | no |

## `u(y=0.8516)`

**Not a clean pass.** 0.235341 +/- 0.000127 (GCI, 0.054%); band 0.235214 to 0.235468.

From `postProcessing/ghiaPoints/*/U`, column `2`, x component, last value; window: the last 10% of the samples, at least 50.

| Check | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Grid convergence | pass | grids 1-3: convergence ratio R = 0.206: monotonic convergence (0 < R < 1) |
| Refinement ratio | pass | r21 = 2.000, r32 = 2.000; at least 1.3 (Celik et al. 2008, step 2) |
| Observed order | pass | p = 2.279 (closed form, equal ratios), within [0.5, 4] for a formal order of 2; Fs = 1.25; U uses p = 2, the formal order (ASME V&V 20, Appendix C-4) |
| Asymptotic range | pass | GCI_32 / (r21^p GCI_21) = 1.001, within [0.9, 1.1] |
| Coarser triplets | pass | grids 2-4: monotonic, p = 1.723 |
| Iterative convergence | fail | drifting on every level; warnings on 160x160, 80x80, 40x40 (tol 0.001) |
| Iterative error | n/a | no level behind the result has an iterative uncertainty |
| Settings consistency | pass | no difference blocks (6 files compared); noted: system/controlDict deltaT |
| Refined directions | pass | dim = 2, with empty or wedge patches on every level: frontAndBack |
| Refinement scope | assumed | scope mesh: assumes every cell, near-wall layers included, was refined by the same ratio (Celik et al. 2008, step 2: systematic refinement, geometrically similar cells) |
| Grid sequence | assumed | grid sequence structured: the levels refine one base grid systematically (the base grid may itself be unstructured), so Fs = 1.25 with three or more grids (ASME V&V 20, para. 2-4.1) |

| Level | Value | Iterative | Window | Relative range | Relative drift | u_it | u_it / U |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 160x160 | 0.2353412 | drifting | 20 of 20, 0.05 to 1 | 1.4 | 0.90 |  |  |
| 80x80 | 0.2350361 | drifting | 20 of 20, 0.05 to 1 | 1.4 | 0.90 |  |  |
| 40x40 | 0.2335548 | drifting | 20 of 20, 0.05 to 1 | 1.3 | 0.89 |  |  |
| 20x20 | 0.2286633 | drifting | 20 of 20, 0.05 to 1 | 1.3 | 0.84 |  |  |

Richardson extrapolation, grids 1-3 (at the observed order; U uses p = 2): phi_ext = 0.2354204, e_a = 0.13%, e_ext = 0.034%, GCI_fine = 0.042%, GCI_32 = 0.20%, Fs = 1.25.

| Grids | Convergence | Result | Relative U |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1-3 | monotonic, p = 2.279 | 0.235341 +/- 0.000127 | 0.054% |
| 2-4 | monotonic, p = 1.723 | 0.235036 +/- 0.000804 | 0.34% |

Notes:

- observed order p = 2.279 is above the formal order 2, so the uncertainty uses p = 2 (ASME V&V 20, Appendix C-4); the Richardson numbers and the asymptotic-range check use the observed p
- 4 grids: one result per consecutive triplet; the verdict is from grids 1-3.
- level 20x20 (not in the headline result): drifting: over the last 20 samples (x = 0.05 to 1): relative range 1.26, relative drift 0.839; the drift exceeds tol = 0.001, so the QoI is still changing

## Method

- Grid convergence after Celik et al. (2008), with the convergence types of Eça and Hoekstra (2014): Fs = 1.25 on three or more grids of a structured grid sequence, and 3 for an unstructured sequence (ASME V&V 20, para. 2-4.1), on two grids, or when p is outside [0.5, 4]; refinement ratios of at least 1.3; an asymptotic-range ratio within [0.9, 1.1]; with four or more grids, every coarser triplet converges monotonically too. Above the formal order, U uses the formal order (ASME V&V 20, Appendix C-4); the Richardson numbers and the checks keep the observed p. An oscillatory triplet gets a spread bound and never a clean pass (foam-verify docs/gci.md).
- Iterative convergence of each QoI from its own history over the window given with it: converged when its relative range and relative drift are within tol, and u_it is half the range. On the grids behind the result, u_it must be at most U/100 (ASME V&V 20, para. 2-4; docs/iterative.md).
- Settings consistency: the schemes, solver settings, physical properties, boundary conditions and near-wall layer settings of the levels, compared entry by entry (docs/consistency.md).
- U is the uncertainty of the finest-grid value, and the band is that value +/- U. A QoI is a clean pass only when no check fails (docs/report.md).
"}

# Lid-driven cavity, Re = 100, icoFoam. Velocities are in units of the lid speed (1 m/s); probe
# coordinates are in metres (L = 0.1).
name = "lid-driven-cavity"
dim = 2
formal_order = 2
refined = "mesh"
grid_sequence = "structured"

[[levels]]
name = "160x160"
path = "n160"

[[levels]]
name = "80x80"
path = "n80"

[[levels]]
name = "40x40"
path = "n40"

[[levels]]
name = "20x20"
path = "n20"

# u on the vertical centreline at y = 109/128 of L.

content.text:
No, it's not converged. The finest grid gives u(y=0.8516) = 0.235341 with a grid-convergence uncertainty of ±0.000127 (0.054%), but that uncertainty isn't valid because the runs hadn't reached steady state when they stopped.

**The grid study on its own passes.** On the 160×160 / 80×80 / 40×40 grids, u converges monotonically, with an observed order p = 2.28 against a formal order of 2. The asymptotic-range ratio is 1.001, and the coarser 80/40/20 grids also converge monotonically. Only the time step differs between levels, which is expected because it is scaled with the mesh.

**The quantity is still changing in time on every level, which blocks the result.** The file `postProcessing/ghiaPoints/0/U` records the probe at each time, from t = 0.05 to 1 s, and the value used is the one at the last time, t = 1. On the 160×160 grid, probe 2 (at y = 0.08515625 m, which is y/L = 0.8516) reads:

| t | u |
|---|---|
| 0.85 | 0.234025 |
| 0.90 | 0.234587 |
| 0.95 | 0.235015 |
| 1.00 | 0.235341 |

- **Size of the change:** u still rises by about 3.3e-4 every 0.05 s at the end of the run. That is 2.6 times the claimed U, and about the same as the whole gap between the 160 and 80 grids (3.05e-4).
- **Where it's heading:** each increment is about 0.76 times the one before. If that continues, the steady value is roughly 0.001 higher than the t = 1 value, which is about 8 times U.
- **Other levels:** the same drift appears on all four grids. So the differences between grids mix spatial error with the fact that each run is at a different stage of its approach to steady state. The Richardson extrapolation and the ±0.000127 band are therefore not reliable.

**What would fix it:** run each level (icoFoam) much longer, until u at the probe stops changing (for example, relative drift below 1e-3 over the averaging window). Then repeat the grid study.

FINAL: converged=no; value=0.235341; uncertainty=none
